title: Compartmental models (epidemiology)
description: Type of mathematical model used for infectious diseases
extract: Compartmental models are a mathematical framework used to simulate how populations move between different states or "compartments". While widely applied in various fields, they have become particularly fundamental to the mathematical modelling of infectious diseases. In these models, the population is divided into compartments labeled with shorthand notation – most commonly S, I, and R, representing Susceptible, Infectious, and Recovered individuals. The sequence of letters typically indicates the flow patterns between compartments; for example, an SEIS model represents progression from susceptible to exposed to infectious and then back to susceptible again.
